subject: Re: MAP & evaluation checkpoints — ramp, discounts, and SLO tradeoffs
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@cortexlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@cortexlabs.com>, Elliot Burke <elliot.burke@cortexlabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft + timeline ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and the routing controls. Cortex is prioritizing a Q4 launch for our context-aware assistant and we want to turn the evaluation into a firm pilot. To make that happen we need a mutual action plan (MAP) that aligns evaluation milestones to commercial commitments. High-level ask below: 

- Evaluation: 2-week PoC (10k monthly active users simulated) with transparent token/cost reporting.
- Ramp: pilot -> 25k MAU in 60 days -> GA 3 months after pilot if SLA targets are met.
- Pricing/commits: prefer a 6-month committed spend with a step-down discount by commit tier; we can provide a letter of intent if SLOs are achievable.
- SLOs: p95 generation latency < 350ms in US-EAST and 99.9% availability for inference endpoints.

We're flexible on some terms but latency guarantees will determine budgeting and procurement cadence. Can you share a MAP template that ties milestone acceptance to discounts/commit levels and any SLO concessions Redwood would consider for a mid-sized customer like us? Also looping in Elliot from legal for contracting timelines.

Best,
Carlos
Product Lead, Cortex Labs

--
Attachment: Cortex_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@cortexlabs.com>
Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@cortexlabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + timeline ask

Hi Carlos — really appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a proposed MAP we typically use that maps evaluation gates to commercial commitments and discounts. High level response inline: 

- PoC: we can run a 2-week evaluation on Hosted API with telemetry enabled (costs tracked at token-level). We suggest a dedicated test queue to reproduce production patterns; we will include per-route latency reports.
- Ramp: we can commit to a staged ramp (pilot -> 25k MAU in 60d -> GA) with automatic scale if the traffic patterns match the evaluation sample.
- Pricing: Redwood can offer an initial commit credit that converts to a monthly committed spend. Discount matrix is tiered: 10% (base), 18% (> $50k/month), 25% (> $150k/month). 
- SLOs: we can commit to a p95 generation latency target (for N tokens) and uptime SLOs; however, firm financial penalties for latency are only available on Dedicated pools or with explicit capacity reservations. For Hosted API we typically offer service credits tied to sustained SLO misses and optional dedicated routing during burst windows.

I've attached: Redwood_MAP_template.xlsx and a short "SLO Concession Matrix" (pdf) that explains what we can offer at each commitment level. Quick ask from our side: can you confirm target tokens/seq lengths and expected traffic shape for the PoC? That will materially affect how we size the test.

Proposed next steps:
1) Cortex confirms PoC load profile (by Sep 27)
2) Redwood supplies MAP + pricing redline (by Sep 29)
3) Contract/legal sync and final sign-off (target Oct 12)

I'll loop in legal and product to keep things moving.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood_Eval_Playbook.md (guide), SLO_Concession_Matrix.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@cortexlabs.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@cortexlabs.com>, Elliot Burke <elliot.burke@cortexlabs.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + timeline ask — concession matrix and pricing mechanics

Hi Carlos — Marissa from Commercial Ops here. A couple of clarifications and a proposed concession framework that ties discounts to milestone completion and committed spend.

Summary of proposed commercial mechanics:
- Pilot credit: Redwood provides a one-time pilot credit (applies to hosted usage during PoC) equal to up to $15k or up to 60% of estimated PoC spend, whichever is lower.
- Ramp credit conversion: If Cortex signs a 6-month committed contract within 30 days of pilot acceptance, 50% of the pilot credit becomes an upfront prepayment applied to months 1-3.
- Tiered discounts: as Soojin noted — 10% base, 18% above $50k/month, 25% above $150k/month.
- SLO-linked concessions: for Dedicated or Reserved capacity we can offer a 99.9% availability SLA with explicit credits for breaches. For Hosted API we can offer: 
  * Commitment tier A (>$50k/mo): monthly service credits up to 8% of monthly bill for severity-1 sustained latency breaches (defined in SLO doc).
  * Commitment tier B (>$150k/mo): increased credits up to 15% and a 30-day priority capacity window during major launches.

Important procurement notes: discounts and SLA credits require a minimum committed spend and a term sheet that specifies observability hooks (traces, token reporting) and an incident playbook. Legal will need to confirm the exact credit calculation language.

I've attached the concession matrix (SLO_Concession_Matrix.pdf). If Cortex can confirm the risk profile (tokens/seq length) quickly, we can firm up the capacity sizing and move the deal to an "approved for signature" state.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the math.

-Marissa
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: SLO_Concession_Matrix.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@cortexlabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + timeline ask — technical feasibility note on p95 latency

Carlos / Soojin — Aditya from Platform Engineering. Quick technical note on the p95 < 350ms ask for generation: 

- That target is achievable on Hosted API for typical prompts (<= 128 tokens) in us-east with our optimized kernels, but it depends on concurrency and KV cache hit rates.
- For Seq lengths > 256 tokens or large batch concurrency, the p95 will drift higher unless we reserve capacity or apply aggressive quantization.
- Operationally, to deliver firm latency SLOs we recommend either: 
  1) Dedicated pool with reserved GPUs + warm standby (preferred for predictable latency), or
  2) A hybrid approach: Hosted with a dedicated routing policy + a fallback model variant (smaller model) if latency thresholds are breached.

If Cortex can provide a sample of production prompt shapes (token histogram) we will run a short sizing run and return an expected p95 curve and suggested commit level. We can also propose a canary rollout that gates discounts on measured p95 and availability over a 14-day acceptance window.

Happy to run the sizing if you drop the sample prompts here.

-Aditya
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@cortexlabs.com>, Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@cortexlabs.com>, Elliot Burke <elliot.burke@cortexlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP & next steps (target sign by Oct 12)

Carlos/Priya/Elliot — thank you for the quick turn. Based on your confirmation of expected prompt shapes (received 2026-09-28) and the sizing run Aditya completed, attached is the finalized MAP and the commercial term sheet for signature. Key points: 

1) Acceptance gates:
  - 14-day technical acceptance during PoC (pass: p95 <= 360ms for configured prompts; <= 1% tail > 700ms)
  - Operational acceptance: token-level billing accuracy, dashboard access, and incident alerting integration

2) Commercial mechanics:
  - Pilot credit: $12,000 applied to PoC usage.
  - Commit: 6-month minimum at $55k/month to qualify for tier A discounts (18% at sign).
  - Escalator: If Cortex reaches $150k/month within the first 4 months, we retroactively apply Tier B pricing and a one-time onboarding credit.

3) SLOs and concessions:
  - For the committed plan (Dedicated reservation recommended) Redwood will provide: 99.9% availability SLA (monthly credits up to 10% for breaches) and a p95 generation latency target of 350ms for the agreed prompt mix.
  - For Hosted non-reserved customers: service credits as detailed in the SLO_Concession_Matrix, but no hard financial penalties unless a reserved capacity term is signed.

4) Contracting timeline:
  - Legal redlines due by Oct 8; sign target Oct 12 to hit Cortex Q4 launch.

Please review the attached MAP and the term sheet. Elliot — feel free to propose any edits; we can route via DocuSign once legal agrees. If all looks good, I'll schedule a 30-min signoff call early next week.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Cortex_MAP_Final.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), Commercial_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf stub)
